title: How 3PL shipping rates work (and how to compare them)
summary: Understand 3PL shipping rates, negotiated pricing, and automated multi-carrier rate shopping. Learn what to compare to uncover savings for your brand.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


- Negotiated 3PL carrier rates depend on your shipment mix and provider terms.
- Dimensions, weight, destination, service level, and fees dictate actual costs.
- Automated multi-carrier rate shopping optimizes shipping option selection.
- Flowspace combines automatic rate shopping in its software with access to high-volume carrier pricing and smarter inventory placement.


A discounted shipping rate can look compelling in a third-party logistics (3PL) proposal, but **the more useful question is what your brand will pay to deliver its actual orders.**


That takes more than reviewing a discount percentage. You need to understand the available carrier pricing, the charges that affect each shipment, and how your fulfillment partner chooses a service when an order is ready to ship.


This guide breaks down how 3PL shipping rates work and how DTC and omnichannel brands can compare U.S. domestic parcel shipping options.


## How do 3PL shipping rates work?


When you ship through a 3PL, you pay transportation charges to move orders from the warehouse to your customers. Your provider may ship using its negotiated carrier rates, your own carrier accounts, or a mix of both. The account used determines which carrier rates apply. Your 3PL may offer better pricing for some shipments, while your own agreement may be more competitive for others.


Shipping is, of course, one part of your 3PL bill. You’ll also pay for services like receiving, storage, pick-and-pack, and packaging. Some providers bundle these costs; others list them separately. Transparent[3PL billing](https://flow.space/blog/3pl-billing) should make it easy to see what you’re paying for, what’s included, and when extra charges apply.


Look for a proposal that spells out your carrier options, how the provider calculates shipping costs, and which fees could increase the final bill. For a broader breakdown, see our guide to[ecommerce fulfillment costs](https://flow.space/blog/ecommerce-fulfillment-costs) .


## How negotiated shipping rates can benefit brands


Negotiated shipping rates are prices established through an agreement with a carrier. A fulfillment provider that ships for multiple brands may use its combined volume to negotiate pricing that an individual brand would struggle to secure alone.


That purchasing power is valuable, especially when a brand’s own volume is limited. But access to a larger shipping base does not guarantee that every shipment will cost less.


The result depends on how the available pricing fits your products, destinations, and delivery requirements. For instance, an agreement that works well for lightweight parcels may offer less value for heavy or oversized orders.


Ask providers to show how their pricing applies to your orders, including any minimum charges and how discounts apply to surcharges. A large discount on a published transportation rate tells you little about fees excluded from that discount.


## What determines your final shipping cost?


Several factors shape the amount you pay:


Shipping cost factors


Cost factor What to evaluate


Weight and dimensions How actual weight, dimensional weight, and package size affect billable weight and handling or oversize fees


Origin and destination Which shipping zones apply and whether the destination triggers a delivery-area surcharge


Service level What each eligible service costs to meet your delivery requirements


Minimum transportation charges Whether a carrier’s minimum charge limits the savings from a negotiated discount


Applicable surcharges Which fuel, residential delivery, handling, seasonal, and other shipment-specific charges apply


Provider billing terms What the quoted price includes, what’s billed separately, and whether the provider adds shipping-related fees


For example,[FedEx explains](https://page.message.fedex.com/weight_calculator/) that when dimensional weight exceeds actual weight, a package can be priced using dimensional weight. A lightweight product in a large box can therefore cost more to ship than its scale weight suggests.


### Compare the full price of the same shipment


Imagine two eligible services for the same package, shipping from the same warehouse to the same customer and meeting the same delivery requirement:


Shipping charge comparison


Shipping charge Option A Option B


Transportation after discount $6.00 $6.75


Combined applicable surcharges $2.50 $1.00


Total shipping cost $8.50 $7.75


Illustrative figures only; these are not carrier quotes or Flowspace rates.


Option B has the higher transportation price but costs $0.75 less overall. Across 10,000 comparable shipments, that difference would total $7,500.


Seasonal fees can change these comparisons further. Our[peak season surcharge guide](https://flow.space/blog/peak-shipping-season) covers that application in detail.


## Why automated multi-carrier rate shopping matters


Multi-carrier rate shopping compares prices across eligible carriers and services for a shipment. Automated rate shopping makes that comparison part of the shipping workflow, with negotiated rates establishing the pricing available to your brand.


The most economical eligible service can change with the package, destination, shipping origin, and delivery requirement. When reviewing a 3PL proposal, ask how the provider compares those options and whether it automates the process for each order.


Flowspace, for example, builds automatic multi-carrier rate shopping into its proprietary[order management platform](https://flow.space/platform/order-management) , comparing carrier rates and service levels as part of fulfillment. That’s a capability worth evaluating alongside the rates in a proposal: how will the provider help your brand put those rates to work?


For brands, this matters in three practical ways:


- **Less manual work:** Teams do not need to compare individual carrier quotes for every order.
- **More precise decisions:** Carrier selection can reflect each shipment rather than relying on one default service for every package.
- **A repeatable process as volume grows:** Automated comparisons make rate shopping practical across thousands of orders.


Delivery requirements still guide the decision. A lower price is useful when the service meets the order’s needs. Ask which services qualify, what delivery rules apply, and which charges the software includes in its comparison.


## How to compare 3PL shipping rates


The most useful comparison starts with your shipment history. Give each provider the same representative sample, including package weights and dimensions, destinations, current shipping costs, and required delivery speeds.


Include the orders that complicate your operation: heavy packages, remote destinations, expedited shipments, and seasonal changes in product mix. A sample consisting only of your easiest orders can hide important cost differences.


### Compare equivalent scenarios


First, compare rates using equivalent origins, packages, destinations, and delivery requirements. Then model the provider’s proposed warehouse placement separately. This lets you distinguish savings from carrier pricing from savings created by shorter shipping distances.


Review the average shipping cost across the sample, weighted by how frequently each shipment type occurs. Break the results down by weight, zone, and service to see where an offer helps—and where it may cost more.


### Ask these questions before signing


- Which carriers and services are available for my products and destinations?
- Is multi-carrier rate shopping automatic, and what rules guide selection?
- Which surcharges are included in quoted rates or rate-shopping comparisons?
- Can I use my own carrier accounts, and are there associated fees?
- Are minimum charges, volume commitments, or separate shipping fees involved?
- How are carrier adjustments and rate changes communicated and billed?
- What shipment-level reporting will help us check quoted costs against actual invoices?


Use the answers to assess both pricing and the process that determines what you pay over time.

## 3PL shipping rates FAQs


### Can a 3PL get better shipping rates?


A 3PL may offer favorable carrier pricing through its combined shipping volume. Whether that pricing improves your costs depends on your shipment profile, current agreements, and the provider’s billing terms. Compare representative orders to assess the difference.


### What is multi-carrier rate shopping?


Multi-carrier rate shopping compares shipping prices across eligible carriers and services for an individual shipment. The comparison should account for the package, destination, and delivery requirements.


### How do negotiated rates and rate shopping work together?


Negotiated rates establish the prices available through carrier agreements. Rate shopping compares eligible options for each shipment. Automation applies that comparison within the shipping workflow.


### Are shipping charges included in 3PL fulfillment fees?


It depends on the provider’s pricing structure. Shipping may appear separately from receiving, storage, handling, and packaging or within a bundled price. Ask for a clear breakdown of included services and additional charges.


### Can brands use their own carrier accounts with a 3PL?


Some providers support a brand’s own carrier accounts. Confirm availability, associated fees, and whether those rates can participate in the provider’s automated rate-shopping process.
